section.title: Remote access (SSH / Telnet)
section.intro: Who may log in over the network, and how. Same settings as ip domain-name, crypto key generate rsa, ip ssh, username and line vty in the CLI.

fields.domainNameHint: Needed for the RSA keys, e.g. lab.local.
fields.keyBitsHint: 360 to 4096; empty = no keys, so SSH is off. 1024 or more is a good choice.
fields.linePasswordHint: Used by the line password check. Empty with that check = remote logins are refused.

loginHints.line: Telnet asks for the line password. SSH needs local users instead.
loginHints.local: Telnet and SSH ask for a user name and password from the list below.
loginHints.none: Telnet gets in without a password. Not safe; SSH still needs local users.

errors.range: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
errors.keysNeedDomain: Set a domain name first: the keys are named after it.
errors.userName: A user name has no spaces.

session.opened: Logged in to {{hostname}} (privilege level {{privilege}}). The remote prompt is not simulated yet, so the session ends here.

cli.vtyOnly: transport input works on the vty lines only (line vty 0 4).

terminal.passwordHint: This terminal cannot ask for a password while the command runs: add it with -pw <password>.
